title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, and ADRs
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview
======

Purpose
-------
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's architecture and standards for API design, code quality, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, and performance engineering, and provides an index of active ADRs (Architecture Decision Records). It is intended as the canonical reference for cross-functional teams building production inference services.

Scope
-----
Applies to all services (hosted API, Dedicated, Private) and components managed by Engineering, SRE, and Applied ML that affect runtime behavior, operational observability, and customer-facing interfaces.

Principles (high-level)
-----------------------
- Predictability: APIs and runtime behavior should be stable and backwards compatible where possible.
- Measurability: Every service must expose metrics, logs, traces, and an SLO.
- Cost-awareness: Design decisions must consider unit economics (tokens/sec, GPU-hours).
- Reproducibility: Model artifacts and infra changes must be versioned with reproducible builds.
- Security-by-default: Least privilege networking and encryption in transit/at rest.

1) API Standards
================
Goal: Provide consistent, discoverable, and versioned HTTP+JSON APIs for models and control-plane features.

Key rules
---------
- API Design: Follow RESTful resource conventions for control-plane endpoints; use HTTP/2+ gRPC for internal high-throughput paths (service-to-service).
- Versioning: All public customer APIs must include explicit version namespaces (e.g., /v1, /v2). Semantic breaking changes require an ADR and a migration plan (deprecation window >= 90 days).
- Error model: Use structured error objects: {"code": string, "message": string, "details": optional object}. Map HTTP codes: 4xx for client errors, 5xx for server failures, 429 for throttling.
- Pagination: Use cursor-based pagination for list endpoints.
- Idempotency: For operations that create state (e.g., create-deployment), support idempotency-key header with 24-hour dedupe window.
- Rate limits & quotas: Expose rate-limit headers (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset). Default throttling policy documented in docs-site.
- Contracts & schemas: All request/response JSON schemas must be maintained in the central OpenAPI registry (see enforcement below).

OpenAPI / schema enforcement
---------------------------
- All public and internal REST endpoints must publish an OpenAPI spec in the central repo (docs/openapi/). CI job "validate-openapi" fails builds when schemas differ from master.
- Example command to validate locally:
  - curl -sS https://git.redwood/internal/openapi/your-service.yaml | swagger-cli validate -

Example public endpoint (short)
-------------------------------
POST /v1/models/{model_id}/generate
Request: application/json
{
  "prompt": "string",
  "max_tokens": 512,
  "stream": false
}
Response 200:
{
  "id": "gen-123",
  "object": "generation",
  "choices": [ { "text": "..." } ]
}

2) Coding Standards
====================
Goal: Maintain consistent, maintainable, and secure code across services.

Languages & style
-----------------
- Primary server languages: Go (control-plane, routing), Python (model adapters, evals), and Rust/C++ for latency-critical runtime kernels.
- Style guides: Use golangci-lint + gofmt for Go; black + ruff for Python. PRs must be lint-clean before merge.

Code review rules
-----------------
1. Two reviewer minimum for any service-level change. At least one reviewer must be from the owning service team.
2. Security-sensitive changes (auth, encryption, network policy) require a security reviewer.
3. Performance-sensitive patches must include a microbenchmark and perf regression target.

Pre-commit & CI
---------------
- Pre-commit hooks: include formatting, basic static checks, and secret scanning. Example .pre-commit-config.yaml snippet in repo root.
- CI gates: unit tests, integration tests (smoke), linting, openapi validation, container image build validation.

Dependency and vulnerability management
--------------------------------------
- Automated dependency scan runs weekly; critical vulnerabilities must be remediated within 7 days.
- Use SBOM for all production images (CycloneDX format).

3) Infrastructure Standards (IaC & Networking)
============================================
Goal: Secure, repeatable provisioning with clear ownership and least privilege networking.

IaC rules
---------
- Terraform is the canonical IaC for cloud resources; modules must live under infra/terraform/modules.
- Module lifecycle: major version bump when module inputs/outputs change in a breaking way; require an ADR for infra module deprecation.
- State management: Remote state in S3 with DynamoDB locking (for AWS). State access limited to infra CI and named oncall roles.

Networking
----------
- VPC-per-environment (prod, staging, dev) with subnet separation for control-plane, GPU-fleet, and management.
- Security groups: deny-by-default; only open narrow ports (gRPC, HTTPS).
- Private endpoints for sensitive services (KMS/HSM, DBs).

Cluster & capacity
------------------
- GPU fleet: Managed as dedicated node pools per instance family and quantization capability. Autoscaling policies belong to eng-infra and SRE.
- CI/CD deploys images into immutable registries (image tags are git-sha).

Example Terraform snippet
------------------------
resource "aws_s3_bucket" "tfstate" {
  bucket = "redwood-tfstate-prod"
  acl    = "private"
}

4) Model-Serving Standards
==========================
Goal: Ensure models are packaged, versioned, and served with predictable performance and safe fallbacks.

Model packaging
--------------
- Model artifacts must be stored in the model registry with metadata: model_id, version, training_commit, tokenizer_spec, quantization_profile (if any), input_signature, output_signature.
- Container image or bundle must be reproducible; include manifest.json with sha256 checksums.

Variant & quantization profiles
------------------------------
- Maintain a set of approved quantization profiles under confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles. Each profile has a validated latency/cost/quality tradeoff.
- Model variants: full-precision, q4_0, q4_1, int8 (if available). Runtime should support graceful fallback between variants.

Rollouts and canaries
---------------------
- Use canary rollouts for any model update: start with 1% traffic for 2 hours, then 10% for 6 hours, then 50% for 24 hours before 100% if no regression.
- Automated quality checks: run evaluation prompt set for new model versions and compare to baseline with statistical thresholds (A/B testing using MQL: p < 0.01 for degradation).

KV cache & session affinity
--------------------------
- For chat/session workloads, persist KV cache per session id with TTL 24h by default. Routing should prefer local cache to avoid cold starts.

Example model manifest (JSON)
---------------------------
{
  "model_id": "redwood-7b-v1",
  "version": "2026-03-01",
  "quantization_profile": "q4_1-latency-optimized"
}

5) Observability Standards
==========================
Goal: Ensure every service is observable and supports SLO-driven alerting and post-incident analysis.

Metrics
-------
- Metrics naming: use dot-separated naming with service prefix: infra.<service>.<metric>. Examples: api.model.generate.latency.p50_ms, api.model.generate.tokens_per_second.
- Required metrics per service: request_count, request_errors (4xx/5xx), latency p50/p90/p99, instance_cpu_utilization, instance_gpu_utilization, queue_length.
- Cardinality: avoid high-cardinality labels in primary counters; use sampling/traces for high-cardinality attributes.

Logs
----
- Structured JSON logs with fields: timestamp, level, service, trace_id, span_id, request_id, user_id (optional), message, attributes (map).
- Retention: 30 days for standard logs, 365 days for audit/security logs (configurable via retention policy).

Tracing
-------
- Use OpenTelemetry for distributed tracing. Trace context must be propagated across HTTP/gRPC boundaries.

Dashboards & Alerts
-------------------
- Baseline dashboard for every service: Overview (traffic, errors, latency), Resource (CPU/GPU/memory), SLO health.
- Alerting policy: Alerts map to runbooks with severity levels (P1, P2, P3).
- Example alert thresholds (API generation service):
  - P1: error_rate >= 2% sustained for 5m AND total_rps > 10 -> Pager (oncall-sre).
  - P1: p99 latency > 3000 ms for 10m -> Pager.
  - P2: cpu_utilization > 90% for 15m -> Slack + Ops; P2 if scaling cannot restore within 10m.

SLOs
----
- Services must define at least one consumer-facing SLO. Example: generation API SLO: availability 99.9% monthly (error_rate < 0.1% by successful response measurement) and latency SLO p90 < 800ms for free-tier models; p90 < 350ms for enterprise-dedicated models.
- Error budget policy: when monthly error budget burned > 50%, freeze non-critical releases and trigger remediation review.

6) Performance Standards & Benchmarking
======================================
Goal: Provide reproducible performance baselines and cost targets for models & runtimes.

Benchmarking suite
------------------
- All runtime changes must include a benchmark run against the canonical perf-suite (eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite). Use continuous perf jobs recorded in the perf-db.
- Bench metrics: tokens/sec per GPU, latency distribution for common sequence lengths (32, 128, 512), memory footprint, throughput at target concurrency.

Targets (example)
-----------------
- Redwood-7B (q4_1) target: 1500 tokens/sec per A100-40GB at batch size 16; p90 latency for 64-token request < 400ms.
- Cost targets are tracked per model in the Optimize dashboard (target cost per 1k tokens).

Regression policy
-----------------
- Any patch that degrades a tracked perf metric by > 5% triggers a rollback candidate and a performance postmortem.

7) ADRs (Architecture Decision Records) index
===========================================
Summary
-------
The following ADRs capture major architecture choices relevant to the standards above. Each ADR includes motivation, alternatives, chosen approach, and migration plan when applicable. Teams must reference ADRs in PRs that affect the decision surface.

Key ADRs (selected)
-------------------
- ADR-2025-01: Default model quantization families (chosen: q4_1 for latency/cost balance).
- ADR-2025-08: API versioning strategy (chosen: explicit /vN namespaces + deprecation windows).
- ADR-2026-02: Service mesh decision (chosen: lightweight sidecar for tracing only; no full mTLS by default inside VPC).
- ADR-2026-06: Runtime kernel selection strategy (chosen: compile-time kernel registry with runtime fallback based on sequence length).

How to author a new ADR
-----------------------
1. Create ADR markdown under docs/adrs/ with filename ADR-YYYY-NN-title.md.
2. Summarize context, alternatives, decision, consequences, and migration plan.
3. Add link to ADR in PR description and update this confluence index.

Governance & Ownership
======================
- Standards owner: Architecture Guild (rotating chairs from eng-platform, eng-infra, eng-serving-runtime).
- Enforcement: CI gates, pre-merge checks, and quarterly architecture reviews.
- Exceptions: Submit a standards-exception request including risk, mitigation, and rollback plan. Exceptions expire after 6 months.

Rollout & Compliance Checklist
=============================
- [ ] OpenAPI spec published and validated in CI.
- [ ] Metrics and tracing added (OTel) with dashboard created.
- [ ] SLO defined and registered in SLO catalog.
- [ ] Load test & perf baseline recorded.
- [ ] Security review completed (if changes to auth/networking).
- [ ] ADR created/updated for architecture-impacting changes.

Runbook & Incident expectations
==============================
- Each service must link to a runbook (eng-platform/runbooks) that maps alerts to playbooks.
- Post-incident: author a 1-pager within 72h and a full incident review within 7 days for P1 incidents.

Appendix: Useful snippets and commands
====================================
- Validate OpenAPI in CI:
  make validate-openapi SERVICE=your-service

- Run local benchmark (example):
  go test ./bench -bench . -benchmem -run TestPerf -args -model redwood-7b -seq 128

- Prometheus alert rule (example):
  - alert: HighErrorRate
    expr: sum(rate(api_model_generate_errors_total[5m])) / sum(rate(api_model_generate_requests_total[5m])) > 0.02
    for: 5m
    labels:
      severity: page
    annotations:
      summary: "High error rate on {{ $labels.service }}"

- Example .pre-commit-config.yaml (snippet):
  repos:
    - repo: https://github.com/psf/black
      rev: stable
      hooks:
        - id: black
    - repo: https://github.com/pycqa/ruff
      rev: stable
      hooks:
        - id: ruff

==================
